punchline: When Barry Schwartz asked for regular jeans, the salesperson had to ask an older colleague what regular jeans used to be.
thirty_sec: Barry Schwartz walks into the Gap and asks for jeans, 32-28. He gets a string of questions back: slim, easy, relaxed, baggy, stonewashed, button-fly. He ends up in the dressing room with one pair of every cut and picks easy fit. The jeans are fine. But a five-minute errand turned into a day of second-guessing, and he now cares about fit in a way he never did before.
